cards.title: Top of the Ladder
cards.instruction: Carry yourself as the highest-status person present. Treat questions as requests for your approval.

cards.title: I’ve Done This Before
cards.instruction: Perform calm familiarity with the task while learning how it works from every new clue.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: I'll decide how we handle this. I'll make your coffee. I know this machine: this button starts it.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: That's steam. The coffee button is behind the flap.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: You can question the details after my decision. Naturally. Steam first, then the concealed coffee controls. Where's your cup?

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Here. It makes two cups unless you turn that dial.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Of course. Dial to one. I always tailor the standard procedure to the guest.

cardFidelity.evidence: A1 and A3 assert decision power, but A5 ordinary familiar-procedure claim does not sustain approval over B instruction.

responseLogic.evidence: B2 steam correction causes A3 revised sequence; B4 dial clue causes A5 one-cup setting, after a question restriction responding to no question.

relationship.evidence: B2 and B4 help operate a specific machine, plausibly teaching A without becoming an adversarial examiner.

heightening.evidence: B4 second control clue requires A5 another immediate adjustment disguised as guest-specific expertise.

specificity.evidence: A1 coffee machine and B2 concealed controls establish the task and observable knowledge gap.

brevityWit.evidence: A5 tailoring-procedure cover is earned by B4 quantity clue, but A3 stock restriction interrupts calm learning.
